long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Doha in January 1952, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani studied at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst and rose through Qatar's armed forces. He became heir apparent and defence minister in 1977, assumed power in 1995 and ruled until voluntarily transferring authority to his son Tamim in 2013. The Amiri Diwan announced his death on 12 July 2026, aged 74.

His reign coincided with the expansion of North Field gas production, the launch of Al Jazeera and the establishment of Qatar Foundation and Qatar Investment Authority. Those were state institutions and national assets, not evidence of his personal ownership. His own wealth is best described as dynastic: Forbes historically estimated a personal fortune and Bloomberg reports extensive Al Thani family wealth, but neither provides a current, auditable breakdown separating his private holdings from state and sovereign assets. The private-wealth industry therefore remains unclassified.

uncertainties: The immutable source record predates the Amiri Diwan's announcement that Sheikh Hamad died on 12 July 2026 and still marks him Alive. The dossier proposes correcting mortality_status to the dataset's Dead option. Because the source-driven inventory classifies blank death-date fields as inapplicable while alive, the exact death day, month and year are recorded in sources and biographies but not proposed as separate fields in this pass.

No exact Forbes profile was found. Forbes published a historical richest-royals slide about Sheikh Hamad, but it is an article rather than a profile and its old personal-fortune estimate does not provide a current asset breakdown.

Qatar's gas resources, QatarEnergy, Qatar Foundation and Qatar Investment Authority are state, public-interest or sovereign institutions. Their assets and achievements were not counted as Sheikh Hamad's private property.

Bloomberg reports extensive Al Thani family wealth and Forbes historically estimated a personal fortune, but neither provides a current, auditable allocation of Sheikh Hamad's individual private holdings. Primary industry is therefore Unknown rather than Energy, Finance & Investments or Diversified.

The source record gives 1 January 1952 as the full birth date, while current official Qatari sources confirm only January 1952. The date was preserved but not newly proposed or used beyond the official month and year.

Reputable reporting attributes Katara to Sheikh Hamad, while SuperYacht Times independently confirms the 124.4-metre vessel without naming its owner. The yacht supports identity resolution but was omitted from the biographies because no strongly sourced personal design or use story was established.

No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or dedicated personal website was found. A low-following LinkedIn name match was rejected because no official source linked to it.
The existing Wikipedia page was preserved as an existing social link but was not used as the sole support for any material claim and may lag the official July 2026 mortality update.
No second nationality was evidenced. Blank suffix and secondary-residence fields were treated as optional, while internal-notes and unknown-name fields were treated as system-controlled.

review.notes: Identity, office history, Doha birthplace and July 2026 death are certain. Reviewer attention is requested for the stale source mortality state, the Royal beneficiary relationship at high rather than very-high confidence and the deliberate Unknown industry classification that excludes Qatari state and sovereign assets.
